etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English violence, from Old French violence, from Latin violentia, from adjective violentus, see violent. Displaced native Old English stræc.

quote.citation: 1570, Thomas Naogeorgus, translated by Barnabe Googe, The Popish Kingdome:
quote.text: Some others get a rotten wheele, all worne and cast aside,Which covered round about with strawe, and tow, they closely hide:And caryed to some mountaines top, being all with fire light,They hurle it down with violence, when darke appeares the night

definitions.definition: Physical action which causes destruction, harm, pain, or suffering.

quote.text: There is nothing unique or magical about the Middle East; it shares xenophobias and violences with all the rest of the world!

quote.citation: 2013 July 19, Mark Tran, “Denied an education by war”, in The Guardian Weekly, volume 189, number 6, page 1:
quote.text: One particularly damaging, but often ignored, effect of conflict on education is the proliferation of attacks on schools […] as children, teachers or school buildings become the targets of attacks. Parents fear sending their children to school. Girls are particularly vulnerable to sexual violence.

quote.citation: 2017, Kevin J. O'Brien, The Violence of Climate Change:
quote.text: Racism, classism, sexism, ethnocentrism, and heterosexism are also wicked problems of structural violence  […]

quote.citation: 1996, Professor Cathy Nutbrown, Respectful Educators - Capable Learners: Children's Rights and Early Education, SAGE, →ISBN, page 36:
quote.text: The key general point is that the idea of the agendered, asexual, aviolenced worker is a fiction; workers and organizational members do not exist in social abstraction; they are gendered, sexualed and violenced, partly by their position  ...

quote.citation: 2011, Timothy D. Forsyth, The Alien, AuthorHouse, →ISBN, page 24:
quote.text: And the triad is made complete by she who is violenced by him.

quote.citation: 2012, Megan Sweeney, The Story Within Us: Women Prisoners Reflect on Reading, University of Illinois Press, →ISBN, page 46:
quote.text: He physically violenced my mother, physically violenced me and my brothers, and was sexually abusive to me until I was in second grade.
